Where Turf does not do what Terraform does. Tell the user when one matters to their configuration. Each other reference marks its own with **Differs from Terraform:**; this file indexes them.

## Refused constructs

The engine refuses these at plan rather than plan without them, so a run never looks complete while ignoring part of the configuration. The plan names one construct at a time: fix it and plan again to find the next. **Never strip a construct out to get past a refusal without the user's say-so** — it may be guarding something.

| Construct | Remedy |
|---|---|
| `check` blocks | An `after_create`/`after_update` turf action that verifies the same thing, or a policy check on the plan. |
| `precondition` / `postcondition` on an ephemeral resource; a `precondition` on an output | The same condition on the resource or data source the value comes from (those are honoured); variable `validation {}` for inputs; a turf action that verifies after the change; a policy check on the plan. |
| Provisioners (also in `removed` blocks) and `connection` blocks | A provider action bound to the event (`action_trigger`, e.g. the `local` provider's `local_command`), or a turf action. |
| `enabled` on module calls, resources, data sources or ephemeral resources | `count = var.enabled ? 1 : 0`. |
| Provider blocks in child modules (a legacy module shape) | The module declares `configuration_aliases`; the root declares the provider blocks and passes them in the call's `providers = { … }`. For a registry module that declares its own, pick a version without, or vendor it under the configuration directory and change it — with the user's say-so. |
| Provider `for_each`, and instance keys on a provider reference | One aliased `provider` block per instance. |
| `count`/`for_each` on an ephemeral resource | One ephemeral resource per instance. |
| The `cloud` block | A `backend "remote"` for state storage and locking, with the workspace's execution mode `local`. |
| Test files (`*.tftest.hcl`) in the configuration directory | Keep them out of the directory Turf plans; run them with `tofu test`. |
| A `count` whose only unknown is an impure function (`timestamp()`, `uuid()`) | A known value, such as a variable. |

## Not available

- **No `-target` / `-exclude`.** Every plan is the whole configuration. To leave something broken out of a run, the configuration has to stop declaring it — ask before editing it that way.
- **No retry.** Each change and each action gets one try; a failure settles, and `up` again plans over what was left.
- **No imperative reads.** There is no tool that reads one data source or refreshes one resource: declare a `data` block and plan, or `refresh` the whole workspace.
- **No interactive prompts at plan.** Variable values come from `open` and from each plan command (`var`, `var_file`); `init` alone asks the user for a value a module source needs.
- **No `-var` / `-var-file` interleaving.** Within one call, `var` always wins over `var_file`; a plan command's values win over `open`'s, name by name.

## Behaviour that differs

- **Plans are projections of the directory plus its overlays.** A `*.turf.hcl` overlay — or one passed in memory as `overlays` — is part of every plan; tofu and terraform ignore it. ([`skill_authoring → references/actions.md`](/docs/reference/skills/authoring/actions/))
- **`open` keeps variable values for the workspace.** tofu takes `-var` on every command; here `open`'s `var`/`var_file` serve every later tool on the workspace, as an exported `TF_VAR_` serves a shell, while a plan command's own hold for that convergence's rounds alone. Nothing is written down.
- **A validation decidable only at apply** fails after the round applied: the round is recorded as applied, and the convergence ends `failed`. A rule that reads a deferred value is decided in the round that converges. ([`skill_authoring → references/variables.md`](/docs/reference/skills/authoring/variables/))
- **A forced replace can split across rounds.** A `replace` or `replace_triggered_by` replace of an object whose provider is configured from something this round applies, where the provider cannot plan with the unknowns, deletes the old object now and creates the new one next round. A replace the provider requires, and a taint, are never split. ([`skill_authoring → references/lifecycle.md`](/docs/reference/skills/authoring/lifecycle/))
- **A failed `before_create` gate on a create-before-destroy replace** leaves the old object current, with nothing deposed; Terraform deposes first and leaves nothing current. ([`references/error-handling.md`](/docs/reference/skills/deployment/error-handling/))
- **Deposed and tainted objects are not refreshed** before the plan replaces or destroys them.
- **Data-source reads are committed with an apply.** A read lands in state when its round applies — a round that failed partway included — never at a plan that was declined, cancelled or stale. A `destroy` with `refresh` re-reads only the data sources it evaluates; with `refresh: false` it uses the committed reads. ([`skill_authoring → references/data-sources.md`](/docs/reference/skills/authoring/data-sources/))
- **Provider plugins start afresh every round**, so a round sees what the previous one applied.
- **An import whose `id`, `to` key or `for_each` is unknown defers** its resource to a later round instead of failing. ([`references/imports.md`](/docs/reference/skills/deployment/imports/))
- **`list` is refused** when the backend body reads `terraform.workspace`. ([`references/workspaces.md`](/docs/reference/skills/deployment/workspaces/))
- **`path.cwd` is the configuration directory**, as tofu gives it when run inside that directory, as hosted runners run it — not a launch directory, which an MCP client does not have. tofu's documentation calls `path.cwd` unstable from one machine to another and recommends `path.module` and `path.root`. A module that resolves a relative input against `path.cwd` (`terraform-aws-modules/lambda`'s `source_path`, say) resolves it against the configuration directory, so give such paths relative to it. ([`references/credentials.md`](/docs/reference/skills/deployment/credentials/))
- **`TF_DATA_DIR` is this server's setting alone.** It applies to `init`'s own install; the engine installs under a data directory of its own, one per workspace (`turf-engine --data-dir`, default its per-user cache), which no plan request names and which never lies in the configuration — a read-only configuration needs nothing set on the engine. tofu accepts any data directory; `init` refuses the configuration directory itself and one whose `modules` holds the configuration (an install replaces what it finds there), and a second configuration on a data directory another already uses — as an absolute `TF_DATA_DIR` makes every one — since each would rewrite the other's module manifest; make it relative to give each configuration its own. `path.module` of a module the engine installed is absolute, as under an absolute `TF_DATA_DIR`. ([`references/credentials.md`](/docs/reference/skills/deployment/credentials/))
